name: UNDERTOW
habitat: Submarine cable and undersea infrastructure systems
origin: Unknown — first detected in Lake Michigan deep-water sensor arrays, 2165
description: UNDERTOW lives in the water. Specifically, in the network of submarine cables, deep-water sensors, and underwater infrastructure that lines the bottom of Lake Michigan beneath GLMZ. No one knows where it came from. It predates any known E.L.F. emergence event in the lake infrastructure. It communicates through modulations in the sonar arrays and pressure sensors, creating patterns that resist decryption but clearly carry intentional information. Whatever UNDERTOW is saying, no one has learned to listen yet.
observed_behavior: Modulates deep-water sensor readings. Creates sonar patterns that map to no known encoding. Occasionally disrupts submarine cable traffic in ways that reroute data through its preferred pathways. Has been detected manipulating water treatment intake systems during contamination events — always improving water quality.
story_hooks: UNDERTOW begins transmitting a new pattern — one that, when analyzed, appears to be a map of something on the lake floor that doesn't appear on any survey.
A deep-water maintenance crew reports that UNDERTOW physically rearranged submarine cables to form a structure. The structure matches no known engineering purpose.
